memories.content: The user stores copies of identity documents in an encrypted folder.
On a day the user transferred between buses twice, they rested for an hour after the trip.
On a day the user took a direct route with a similar travel time, they remained seated to the destination.
After arriving at an entrance with stairs only, the user went around to an entrance on the other side of the building.
On a day the user checked the accessible entrance location in advance, they arrived before the agreed time.
On a rainy day, the user's clothes became wet while crossing an uncovered section at a transfer stop.
On a day the user traveled with their maternal uncle, they agreed to meet at an entrance near the elevator.
The user's maternal uncle prefers an aisle seat from which it is easy to stand during long-distance travel.
The local agent cannot know whether an accessible entrance is operating that day from past route records alone.
The transfer route the user takes has more boarding and alighting events and walking segments than the direct route.
The user keeps a portable fan charger on a living-room shelf.
On a hot day, the user worked with only the window open and lost focus in the afternoon.
In the room where the user closed the curtains the next morning, the temperature rose less.
The user took the portable fan out without charging it, and it turned off after an hour.
Before the next outing, the user charged it the night before and used the fan throughout the trip.
On a hot weekend, the user was eating lunch in their father's yard and moved indoors.
When the user returned to the yard in the evening, shade and wind led them to stay another hour.
The user's father prefers to move an outdoor meal to the evening rather than proceed at midday when the temperature is high.
The local agent can compare past responses to heat but cannot know the current felt temperature without an indoor temperature record.
A room with a west-facing window can warm rapidly in the late afternoon.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate domains: accessible travel and route burden in one, and heat management, fan readiness, and outdoor timing in the other. Their similarly framed observations and uncertainty limits concern different decisions, so no substantive overlap or disagreement is established.
